title: The Danish Gambit
description: Hyper-aggressive and tricky TRIPLE pawn gambit. If you're below 1500, this could score you some very crushing victories. Otherwise, the positions are fun and full of attacks.

r1bqkbnr/ppp2ppp/2np4/8/2B1P3/5N2/PB3PPP.text:
Black develops their knight towards the center.

We'll castle into safety before starting to attack.

r2nkb1r/pppq1ppp/3p1n2/8/2B1P1b1/1Q3N2/P.text:
Black retreats the knight to protect both pawns. However, this reduces Black's central influence.

Hence we'll take advantage of this and start to open up the center with the pawn thrust e5.

r2nkb1r/pppq1ppp/3p4/4P2n/2B3b1/1Q3N2/PB.text: We'll bring the other rook into play. Now we're threatening unpleasant discovered checks on the e-file. Black is already in trouble.
Black is trying to keep the central files closed and moves the knight away from the attack.

r2nkb1r/pppq2pp/3ppn2/6N1/4PP2/1Q6/PB1N2.text: We are not interested. We prefer to finish development, and we're now ready to go after the black king.

r2nkb1r/pppq2pp/3ppn2/6N1/4PP2/1Q6/PB4PP.text: Black develops the knight, making a trade of bishop for knight possible.

r2nkbnr/pppq2pp/3pp3/6N1/4P3/1Q6/PB3PPP/.text:
Black retreats the Knight and protects both b7 and e6.

Now we'll start pushing the f-pawn, intending to open the f-file for our rook in the future.

r2qkbnr/ppp2ppp/2np4/8/2B1P1b1/5N2/PB3PP.text:
Black develops the light-squared bishop and pins the knight on f3.

We'll develop our queen's knight, adding support to the knight on f3. 

By choosing d2 rather than c3, we also keep the diagonal open for our strong b2-bishop.

r2qkbnr/ppp2ppp/2npb3/8/2B1P3/5N2/PB3PPP.text:
Black develops the light-squared bishop and offers a piece trade, hoping to reduce the pressure, even if just a bit.

We'll accept, because it allows us to create weak squares around the black king.

r2qkbnr/ppp3pp/2npp3/8/4P3/5N2/PB3PPP/RN.text:
Black has to recapture. Otherwise, they have lost a whole piece.

Now we'll bring our queen out, forking b7 and e6.

r3kb1r/ppp2qpp/3p1n2/n7/4P1b1/1Q3N2/PB1N.text: Black has no better choice than to capture.

r3kb1r/ppp2qpp/3p1n2/nQ6/4P1b1/5N2/PB1N1.text:
We fork the king and the loose knight. 

This wins the piece back and the black king is going to be very unsafe in the center.

r3kb1r/pppq1ppp/2np1n2/8/2B1P1b1/5N2/PB1.text:
Black decides to wait and develop their kingside first.

We'll bring our queen out, connecting the rooks and attacking b7 and f7.

r3kb1r/pppq1ppp/3p1n2/n7/2B1P1b1/1Q3N2/P.text:
Black forks the queen and bishop, hoping they can release the pressure by trading off the strong light-squared bishop.

We now have a clever tactic to take advantage of the undefended Knight on a5. We'll temporarily sacrifice a piece on f7!

r3kbnr/pppq1ppp/2np4/8/2B1P1b1/5N2/PB1N1.text:
Black develops the queen and prepares to castle queenside.

We'll immediately put our rook on the c-file so that it will be eyeing the enemy king if they castle long.

r3kbnr/pppq2pp/2npp3/8/4P3/1Q3N2/PB3PPP/.text:
Black decides to protect the pawn that is guarding the king.

We're not interested in side pawns!

The knight is going straight for the black king, threatening to capture on e6 and remove this very important defender.

rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/3p4/8/2B1P3/8/PB3PPP/RN.text:
Black is starting to open up their pieces.

We'll continue to develop and prepare to castle.

rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R.text:
The most popular reply for Black.

We'll strike immediately in the center, threatening to win the e5-pawn.

rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/8/2B1P3/8/Pp3PPP/RNB.text:
Black has won a few pawns, but they have given us two very strong bishops on open diagonals.

We recapture, bringing the bishop to the long a1-h8 diagonal, from where it will harass Black's kingside.

rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/8/3pP3/8/PPP2PPP/RNB.text:
Black's best option is to immediately eliminate our perfect center.

We have no intention of recapturing on d4. Instead, we are going to sacrifice another pawn in order to gain much quicker development.

rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/8/4P3/2p5/PP3PPP/RNB.text:
Black is greedy and grabs another pawn.

We'll ignore this and develop the bishop to attack f7 immediately.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK.text:
Welcome to the Danish Gambit! 

It's one of those gambits that's better for Black to decline and just play solidly.

Here, White plays 2.d4 and sacrifices both d4 and c3, and sometimes also the pawn on b2. 

But don't fear, because White gets such an initiative that Black often has to give it all back with interest.

We'll get started with 1.e4.

r1bqk1nr/ppp2ppp/2np4/8/1bB1P3/2N2N2/PB3.text:
Black opens up the light-squared bishop and fortifies the e5-square.

White brings the queen out, puts pressure on the dark-squared bishop and eyes the f7-square.

r1bqk1nr/pppp1ppp/2n5/8/1bB1P3/5N2/PB3PP.text:
Black develops the dark-squared bishop with check.

White blocks the check and develops the last minor piece.

r1bqkbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/8/2B1P3/8/PB3PPP/R.text:
Black develops a knight towards the center.

White brings another minor piece out and prepares to castle.

r2qk1nr/ppp2ppp/2npb3/8/1bB1P3/1QN2N2/PB.text:
Black develops their light-squared bishop and offers White one of their pawns back in exchange for quicker development.

We may as well accept the offer.

r2qk1nr/ppp3pp/2npp3/8/1b2P3/1QN2N2/PB3P.text:
Black has to recapture. Otherwise, they have lost a piece.

White puts the King into safety.

r3k1nr/pppq2pp/2npp3/3N4/1b2P3/1Q3N2/PB3.text:
A clever tactic, using the fact that the dark-squared bishop is only protected by the knight. 

If Black takes the knight, the e-file will open up and the black knight will be attacked. If it moves, the bishop falls, so White gains their piece back with excellent attacking possibilities.

r3k1nr/pppq2pp/2npp3/8/1b2P3/1QN2N2/PB3P.text: Black develops the queen, protects e6 and potentially prepares queenside castling.

rnb1k1nr/ppppqppp/8/8/1bB1P3/2N5/PB3PPP/.text:
Black gets the queen out and attacks e4, thanks to the pin on c3.

We'll block the e-file and add support to c3. We're not scared of Black taking on e4 because we can respond with Qb3, hitting both b4 and f7.

rnb1k1r1/ppp2pPp/8/3N4/2p5/8/P4PPP/3RK1N.text:
We centralize the knight and take advantage of the weak c7-pawn. Whenever the queen leaves d8, the c7-pawn becomes weak.

Additionally, we are threatening a fork with Nf6+. Black is completely lost.

rnb1k1r1/ppp2pPp/8/8/2p5/2N5/P4PPP/3RK1N.text: Black moves the rook out of the attack and intends to regain the pawn at some point.

rnb1k2r/ppp2pPp/8/8/2p5/2N5/P4PPP/R2qK1N.text:
Black decides to trade the queens in order to release the pressure on their king.

We'll recapture the queen and bring the rook into play.

rnb1k2r/ppppqppp/5n2/8/1bB1P3/2N5/PB2NPP.text: We castle into safety and are now ready to connect the rooks and start harassing Black on the half-open c- and d-files.
Black refuses to take the "free" pawn and correctly decides to get another minor piece out.

rnb4r/ppp2kpp/5n2/8/4P3/8/PB1N1PPP/R3K1N.text: We recapture the bishop and develop the knight. In the next few moves, we'll finish our development and get the king castled into safety. Afterwards, we will most likely start pushing our kingside pawns in order to use the passed pawn on the e-file.

rnb4r/ppp2kpp/5n2/8/4P3/8/PB1b1PPP/RN2K1.text: Black has to take the queen and recover the material.

rnbQ3r/ppp2kpp/5n2/8/1b2P3/8/PB3PPP/RN2K.text:
Black develops the bishop with check, opening up the eighth rank so that they can regain the lost material.

We must retreat our queen to block the check, otherwise we would simply lose the queen for nothing.

rnbk1b1r/ppp2ppp/5P2/8/2p5/8/PB3PPP/RN2K.text:
Black has to recapture.

We'll capture on g7, destroying Black's kingside pawn structure, and acquiring a dangerous pawn on the seventh.

rnbk3r/ppp2pPp/8/8/1bp5/8/PB3PPP/RN2K1NR.text:
Black develops the bishop with check. This is the only way to escape loss of material.

We'll block the check and develop the knight.

rnbkr3/ppp2pPp/8/8/1bp5/2N5/PB2NPPP/R3K2.text:
We block the check and develop our last minor piece.

The black king is dangerously exposed and our pawn on g7 is a permanent danger.

rnbkr3/ppp2pPp/8/8/1bp5/2N5/PB3PPP/R3K1N.text: Black moves the rook out of the attack with check.

rnbq1b1r/ppp2kpp/5n2/8/4P3/8/PB3PPP/RN1Q.text:
Black is not giving up the queen - they are going to get it back using a discovered attack.

We capture on d8.

rnbq1rk1/pppp1ppp/5n2/8/2B1P3/2Q2N2/PB3P.text:
We develop the last minor piece and are now ready to castle and connect the rooks. 

Afterwards, we can start a pawn avalanche with f2-f4 and e4-e5 in order to take advantage of the active placement of our pieces.

rnbq1rk1/pppp1ppp/5n2/8/2B1P3/2Q5/PB3PPP.text: Black gets the king out of the middle.

rnbqk1nr/pppp1ppp/8/8/1bB1P3/8/PB3PPP/RN.text:
Black develops the bishop with check.

We'll block the check and develop the knight.

rnbqk1r1/ppp2pPp/8/8/2p5/2N2Q2/P4PPP/R3K.text:
We develop the queen, eyeing f7 and b7. This is important because it stops the light-squared bishop from coming out. 

Furthermore, now that the queen has left d1, the square is free for the rook.

rnbqk1r1/ppp2pPp/8/8/2p5/2N5/P4PPP/R2QK1.text: Black moves the rook out of the attack, intending to regain the pawn at some point.

rnbqk2r/ppp2ppp/5P2/3p4/1bB5/8/PB3PPP/RN.text:
Black develops the bishop with check and will regain the lost material in the next couple of moves.

We'll block the check, forcing the exchange of bishops which will bring our knight into the game.

rnbqk2r/ppp2ppp/5P2/3p4/2B5/2b5/P4PPP/RN.text:
Black has to take in order to avoid losing material.

We'll recapture the piece and develop the knight.

rnbqk2r/ppp2ppp/5P2/8/2p5/2N5/P4PPP/R2QK.text:
Black finally regains the piece, but now their king is very exposed.

We'll capture on g7, forcing the black rook to move. Black loses the right to castle kingside.

rnbqk2r/pppp1ppp/5n2/8/1bB1P3/2N5/PB3PPP.text:
Black develops the king's knight, hitting e4 due to the pin on c3.

We'll bring the queen out and threaten both b4 and f7.

rnbqk2r/pppp1ppp/5n2/8/2B1P3/1Qb5/PB3PPP.text:
Black is basically forced to take on c3. Otherwise, they would lose the important f7-pawn and their king would be exposed.

We'll recapture with the queen, creating a powerful battery on the long diagonal. 

After Black has castled, we may have serious threats along this diagonal.

rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/5P2/8/2p5/8/PB3PPP/RN1Q.text:
Black regains the piece and offers a trade of queens, hoping to release the pressure and make their king a bit safer.

We'll accept the trade in order to take away Black's castling rights.

There are still a lot of pieces on the board and both central files are open, therefore it is a good idea.

rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/5n2/3B4/4P3/8/PB3PPP/RN.text:
Black develops the knight, but does not do anything to stop our threat.

We'll use the clever Bxf7+ tactic to fully regain our material.

rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/5n2/3pP3/2B5/8/PB3PPP/R.text:
Black counterstrikes in the center and blocks the a2-g8 diagonal.

We are happy to open up the central files due to better development, so we'll take on f6.

rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/5n2/8/2B1P3/8/PB3PPP/R.text:
Black develops their knight and attacks e4.

We'll push the pawn forward, claiming more space and attacking the knight.

rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/3p4/2B1P3/8/PB3PPP/RN.text:
Black gives one pawn back in order to gain time to open up their light-squared bishop.

We'll capture with the bishop, keeping the a2-f7 diagonal open. Note that we are now threatening to capture on f7, due to the black king being overloaded.

rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R.text:
The most popular reply for Black.

We'll strike immediately in the center, threatening to win the e5-pawn.

rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/8/2B1P3/8/Pp3PPP/RNB.text:
Black has won a few pawns, but they have given us two very strong bishops on open diagonals.

We finally recapture, bringing the bishop to the long a1-h8 diagonal, from where it will harass Black's kingside.

rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/8/3pP3/8/PPP2PPP/RNB.text:
Black's best option is to immediately eliminate our perfect center.

We have no intention of recapturing on d4. Instead, we are going to sacrifice another pawn in order to gain much quicker development.

rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/8/4P3/2p5/PP3PPP/RNB.text:
Black is greedy and grabs another pawn.

We'll develop the bishop and attack f7 immediately.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK.text:
In the second study of this course, we're going over more lines in the Danish Gambit Accepted. 

After Black accepts all three free pawns, at move 5 they have several possible moves. 

In the previous study we saw 5...d6. 

Here, we're going over other natural moves, such as Nc6 and Bb4+.

Let's get started with 1.e4.

2kr2nr/ppp2ppp/2n5/3q4/1b1P2b1/2N2N2/PP2.text:
Black brings their king into safety and activates the rook. 

Furthermore, they are adding pressure on d4.

We'll castle, unpinning the knight, and thus attacking the queen on d5.

2kr2nr/ppp2ppp/2n5/q7/1b1P2b1/2N1BN2/PP2.text:
We'll ignore c3, developing the bishop to defend e3. 

If Black decides to take on c3 and gain a pawn, we will then gain control of the half-open b- and c-files, which lead directly to the black king.

2kr2nr/ppp2ppp/2n5/q7/1b1P2b1/2N2N2/PP2B.text: Black removes the queen from the knight attack and adds pressure on c3.

r1b1kbnr/ppp2ppp/2n5/3q4/3P4/8/PP3PPP/RN.text:
Black develops a knight and attacks d4.

We'll develop the king's knight and add protection to our d-pawn.

r3k1nr/p1p2ppp/2p5/8/1b1P4/2N5/PP2KPPP/R.text: White has to recapture with the king. Even though this relinquishes castling rights, it is not a problem because this position is very close to an endgame, and in endgames, the king should normally be as close to the center as possible.

r3k1nr/p1p2ppp/2p5/8/1bqP4/2N5/PP3PPP/R1.text:
Black recaptures the bishop with the pawn because they want the queen to stay on c4, preventing us from castling.

We'll release the pressure by forcing a queen trade.

r3k1nr/ppp2ppp/2n5/3q4/1b1P2b1/5N2/PP2BP.text:
Black develops the dark-squared bishop with check. 

Black didn't fall for ...Bxf3 8.Bxf3 Qxd4 "winning" the d-pawn, but losing the queen after 9.Bxc6+.

We'll block the check and develop the knight.

r3k1nr/ppp2ppp/2n5/3q4/1b1P4/2N2b2/PP2BP.text:
Black eliminates the defender of d4 and lures the bishop away from the f1-a6 diagonal.

We'll recapture with the bishop, preventing Black from winning the d-pawn.

r3k1nr/ppp2ppp/2n5/8/1bqP4/2N2B2/PP3PPP/.text:
Black uses the fact that White has moved the bishop away to add more pressure on c3.

We'll eliminate the c6-knight in order to reduce the pressure on d4.

r3k2r/ppp2ppp/2n2n2/3q4/1b1P2b1/2N2N2/PP.text:
Black develops their last minor piece and protects the bishop on g4.

We'll castle into safety.

r3k2r/ppp2ppp/2n2n2/q6b/1b1P4/2N2N1P/PP2.text:
Black does not want to trade on f3 so they move the bishop away, but they stay on the same diagonal.

We'll develop the bishop and add protection to d4.

r3k2r/ppp2ppp/2n2n2/q7/1b1P2b1/2N2N2/PP2.text:
The black queen was hanging on d5, so it moves sideways and brings pressure to bear on c3.

Now we'll attack the black bishop and also open up space for our king so that back rank checkmates won't be an issue in the future.

r3kbnr/ppp2ppp/2n5/3q4/3P2b1/5N2/PP3PPP/.text:
Black develops a bishop and pins the knight on f3. 

The threat is to capture the knight and then capture on d4.

We'll develop the light-squared bishop, breaking the pin.

r4rk1/ppp2ppp/2n2n2/q6b/1b1P4/1QN1BN1P/P.text: White develops the queen and protects c3. Also, there is an unpleasant x-ray for Black on the b-file.

r4rk1/ppp2ppp/2n2n2/q6b/1b1P4/2N1BN1P/PP.text: Black puts their king into safety.

rnb1kbnr/ppp2ppp/8/3q4/3p4/2P5/PP3PPP/RN.text:
Black recaptures the pawn and centralizes their queen.

We'll regain the pawn and free c3 for our knight.

rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/8/3p4/3pP3/2P5/PP3PPP/R.text:
Black knows that by accepting the sacrifice, they would be giving White too much piece activity. 

Therefore, they decide to strike back in the center and open up their pieces instead.

We'll take on d5, solving the challenge to our e-pawn.

rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R.text:
The most popular reply for Black. 

We'll strike immediately in the center, threatening to win the e5-pawn.

rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/8/3pP3/8/PPP2PPP/RNB.text:
Black's best option is to eliminate our perfect center.

We have no intention of recapturing on d4. Instead, we are going to sacrifice another pawn in order to gain much quicker development.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK.text:
Another approach Black could go for is 3...d5. 

Basically, they don't buy into our gambit and they prefer to just open up their position. 

Let's see how to deal with this, beginning with 1.e4!

r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2np4/3nP3/3P4/5N2/PP3PP.text:
Black develops the knight and puts more pressure on the center.

We'll get the light-squared bishop out, pinning the knight on c6.

r2qkb1r/pppb1ppp/2n5/1B2p3/3P4/2P2N2/P4P.text:
We ignore e5 and put our king into safety. Re1 is an idea here.

In the next few moves,we will recapture on e5 and develop the dark-squared bishop. After that, we may well begin attacking on the kingside. 

Black should hurry to castle, or else...

Black eliminates the e-pawn and opens up their dark-squared bishop.

If Black tries the previously mentioned tactic with 9...Nxe5, we have 10.Qe2! regaining the pawn after 10...Bxb5 11.Qxb5+ Nd7 12.Qxb7.

r2qkb1r/pppb1ppp/2np4/1B1nP3/3P4/5N2/PP3.text:
Black breaks the pin and threatens a tactic with ...Nxe5.

We'll protect the bishop, thus avoiding the ...Nxe5 trick.

r2qkb1r/pppb1ppp/2np4/1B2P3/3P4/2n2N2/PP.text:
Black refuses to retreat the knight and decides to trade it off instead.

We'll recapture, creating a pawn chain in the center and opening up both the b-file and the dark-squared bishop.

rnb1k2r/ppp1qppp/8/3p4/1b1P4/2NBPN2/PP1Q.text: Black finally opens up the light-squared bishop and stops the white e-pawn from advancing.

We put the king into safety and finish our development. 

In the next few moves, we should bring the a-rook to the e-file and open up the center to use the fact that Black's queenside is still asleep.

rnb1k2r/pppp1ppp/5n2/8/1b1Pq3/2N1B3/PP3P.text:
Black protects the queen by pinning the knight on c3.

We'll develop the other knight and we are close to castling. 

In contrast, Black's queenside is still undeveloped.

rnb1k2r/pppp1ppp/8/3n4/1b1Pq3/2N1BN2/PP3.text:
Black adds more pressure on c3 (and to e3), but neglects their development.

We'll develop the queen, adding protection to c3.

rnb1k2r/pppp1ppp/8/8/1b1Pq3/2N1nN2/PP1Q1.text:
Black trades off our dark-squared bishop, but that is completely fine because the bishop was very restricted anyway.

We'll recapture with the pawn and open up the f-file.

rnb1k2r/ppppqppp/8/8/1b1P4/2N1PN2/PP1Q2P.text:
Black has to retreat the queen, now that the knight on c3 is no longer pinned.

We'll develop the last minor piece, eyeing h7.

rnb1kb1r/pppp1ppp/5n2/8/3Pq3/4B3/PP3PPP/.text:
Black develops a knight towards the center, intending to castle as soon as possible.

We'll develop a knight, attacking the black queen.

rnb1kbnr/pppp1ppp/8/8/3Pq3/8/PP3PPP/RNBQ.text:
Black captures a pawn with check, but now their queen is very exposed.

We'll block the check and develop our queen's bishop.

rnb1kbnr/ppppqppp/8/8/3pP3/2P5/PP3PPP/RN.text:
Black ignores the pawn on c3 and focuses on e4 instead.

We'll capture on d4, freeing c3 for the knight.

rnb2rk1/ppp1qppp/5n2/3p2B1/1b1P4/2NB1N2/.text:
We free the e-file for the rook and pin the knight on f6. 

Note that the d5-pawn is now hanging because of the pin. Black will struggle to counter all White's threats and to get good development.

rnb2rk1/ppp1qppp/5n2/3p4/1b1P4/2NBBN2/PP.text: Black opens up the light-squared bishop and takes control of e4, where they could place their knight in the future.

rnb2rk1/pppp1ppp/5n2/8/1b1Pq3/2N1BN2/PP3.text:
Black castles their king into safety.

We'll develop the last minor piece with an attack on the black queen.

rnb2rk1/ppppqppp/5n2/8/1b1P4/2NBBN2/PP3P.text:
Black retreats the queen so that it cannot be harassed further.

We'll castle and get our king into safety.

rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/3p4/3nP3/3P4/8/PP3PPP/R.text:
Black opens up the light-squared bishop and challenges the annoying e5-pawn which is inhibiting their development.

We'll add support to the central pawns, developing the knight at the same time.

rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/5n2/8/3pP3/2P5/PP3PPP/.text:
Black develops the knight and hits e4.

We'll kick the knight away and gain space in the center.

rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/8/3nP3/3p4/2P5/PP3PPP/.text:
Black centralizes the knight.

We'll regain the pawn, freeing c3 for our knight.

rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R.text:
The most popular reply for Black. 

We'll strike immediately in the center, threatening to win the e5-pawn.

rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/8/3pP3/8/PPP2PPP/RNB.text:
Black's best option is to immediately eliminate our perfect center.

We have no intention of recapturing on d4. Instead, we are going to sacrifice another pawn in order to gain much quicker development.

rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/8/4P3/2PB4/PP3PPP/RN.text:
We recapture the pawn and develop the bishop. 

Even though the dark-squared bishop will not get the chance to occupy the a1-h8 diagonal, we are still doing fine.

We will castle, finish our development and then probably try to create pressure along the half-open d-file.
